title: Embed postmortem-driven SLO & fallback requirements into runtime PRD
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: After the 2026-02-28 regional runtime incident (EU-west latency storm) the postmortem prioritized several actionable reliability changes that must be translated into the runtime PRD. This ticket captures scope changes, clarified requirements, and concrete acceptance criteria so engineering, design, and SRE can implement predictable fallbacks and observable SLO enforcement for production inference.

Problem observed: During the incident automated routing and fallback decisions were inconsistent across routes, leading to partial degradations without clear rollback triggers. Runbook steps were ambiguous and dashboards lacked route-level latency budgets.

PRD changes requested (high level):
- Add a dedicated "SLO & Fallbacks" section that defines per-route latency and error SLOs, error-budget burn actions, and explicit fallback chains for model variants.
- Define control-plane APIs and flags required to opt routes into "strict fallback" vs "best-effort fallback" behaviors.
- Require canary gating with traffic-shift automated checks and rollback triggers tied to SLO violations.
- Add required observability artifacts: dashboard templates, alert thresholds, and post-incident diagnostics (trace links, KV cache hit rates).
- Include acceptance tests (integration + chaos) and a verified runbook with on-call playbooks for degraded latency scenarios.

Scope changes / trade-offs:
- In-scope: PRD text updates, API contract additions, acceptance test definitions, dashboard alert spec, rollout gating workflows, and signoff criteria.
- Out-of-scope for this ticket: low-level kernel scheduling changes and hardware provisioning (these are tracked in ENG dependencies).
- Trade-offs: tighter SLOs and stricter fallbacks will increase short-term operational cost (more fallback invocations, potential higher model cost) and may impact latency tails for some low-priority customers; justified by reducing high-severity outages and predictable customer experience.

Deliverables:
- Updated PRD document with SLO tables, fallback sequences, control-plane API examples, and rollout acceptance criteria. (Confluence draft link included in comments)
- Acceptance criteria checklist (below) and test plan for Eng/SRE to validate.
- Design wireframes for Console UX changes to expose per-route SLOs and manual override controls.
- Linked ENG work items for implementation and a gated release plan.

Stakeholders: Product (Maya Chen), Runtime Eng (Rafael Ortiz, Eng Lead), SRE (Priya Malhotra), Design (Liam Park), QA (Nora Ibrahim).

Timeline: Rough target for PRD finalization and stakeholder signoff by 2026-03-31 to align with runtime-1.22 planning window.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route SLO matrix added to PRD with numeric targets (p50/p95/p99 latency and error-rate SLOs) and documented error-budget actions.
Fallback chains defined (primary model -> reduced-context variant -> cached response -> safe default) with deterministic selection rules and priority order.
Control-plane API spec added with example payloads for toggling fallback behavior and canary gates; API review completed by ENG.
Canary gating procedure documented: automated checks, rollback triggers, and minimum telemetry coverage; must include a chaos test scenario that reproduces reduced throughput.
Console mockups showing per-route SLO display and manual override control accepted by Design and reviewed in PRD notes.
A runbook for degraded-latency incidents added and validated in one tabletop drill with SRE within the release window.
Dashboards and alerts defined (traces, KV cache hit rate, inter-region RTT, model latency by token) and linked to PagerDuty playbooks.
All new requirements linked to ENG-4123 and ENG-4199 and at least one implementation PR opened before the PRD signoff date.
Acceptance tests (integration + chaos) added to the test harness and pass in CI for a canary release candidate.
